oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • Dedicated pool autoscale anomaly detected for pool dedicated-west-2-gpu. Router fallback loop observed. Paging oncall. Incident link: https://redwood.incidents/1987654321 :rotating_light:

alejandra: I'm on it — pulling runbook and metrics. I can see router metric `active_capacity` dropped to 0 at 19:04 UTC and router started returning 503 -> fallback attempts skyrocketed.

samir: I see the autoscaler emitted desired=0 for that pool. Exporter reported `gpu_utilization = NaN` then the scaler interpreted it as zero demand. Running quick check: `curl -s http://autoscaler.local/metrics | grep dedicated-west-2` -> got `desired_replicas{pool="dedicated-west-2-gpu"} 0`.

maria-g: If desired=0 is wrong we should pause autoscaler before we do other changes to avoid oscillation. Alejandra, can you try pause?

alejandra: Pausing now — `POST /autoscaler/pause?pool=dedicated-west-2-gpu` -> 200 OK. Confirmed: autoscaler state=PAUSED.

samir: Good. Now we need to restore capacity to stop the blackholing. I'll scale the pool manually to 4 replicas. `kubectl -n infra scale deploy/dedicated-west-2 --replicas=4`

jake: Heads up — the router's fallback policy has been aggressively routing to cross-region fallback variants. That made traffic bounce between pools when capacity changed, causing a feedback loop. We should disable auto-variant fallback temporarily.

ryan: I'm flipping the router policy flag `auto_variant_fallback` -> false for the affected service. Command: `routerctl config set svc/auth-service auto_variant_fallback=false --scope=pool:dedicated-west-2`. Applying now.

casey: Manual scale succeeded, pods are Ready. Starting traffic drain probe. `kubectl get pods -l app=dedicated-west-2 -o wide` shows 4/4 ready.

cs-eli: CS update: impacted customers reported elevated errors: acme-co, buildly, and three smaller accounts. Estimated failed requests ~14k over last 12m, error rate peaked at 6.2% for routed text generation. Flagging for SRE postmortem and a customer communications touchpoint.

maria-g: We're going to pin the model variant for in-flight routes to avoid cross-variant retries. Jake, can you set force-variant to `redwood-v1-quant` for the route?

jake: Done: `routerctl route update --id=route-842 --force_variant=redwood-v1-quant`. Confirmed. This prevents router from attempting variant fallbacks.

samir: Observability note — the exporter (gpu-metrics-exporter v0.9.1) returned malformed metrics for ~90s. Likely root cause. Temporarily reverted exporter image to v0.9.0 on dedicated-west-2.

alejandra: Handoff: I'm handing primary oncall to Samir at 19:35 UTC while I rotate to incident commander for customer comms. Samir, you're primary for remediation.

samir: Taking over primary. My immediate actions: 1) keep autoscaler paused, 2) keep router fallback off, 3) monitor latencies and error rates, 4) coordinate with runtime to fix exporter.

ops-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP COMPLETED • Pause autoscaler (step 2) — verified by runbook.

ryan: After disabling fallback and scaling, 5m windows show error rate falling to 0.6% and tail latency improved. No new 503s from dedicated-west-2.

cs-eli: Customer impact note added to incident page. I'll prepare a short status blurb for affected customers and loop in account owners.

eng-manager-liz: This is P1. Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime to investigate exporter regression, eng-platform to add fallback circuit-breaker, and devex to improve runbook guidance on scaler pause.

casey: Quick verification — traffic is draining back into pool normally, router metrics `fallback_attempts` back to baseline.

ops-runbook-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED • autoscaler resumed on safe metric (gauge) with hotfix deployed to exporter; router fallback policies restored to default at 19:52 UTC. Please file postmortem and RCA.

alejandra: Marking resolved from oncall perspective. Samir — handoff complete, adding you to follow-ups for the eng-runtime RCA.

samir: Acknowledged. I'll own the RCA and follow-ups. Tentative root cause: exporter v0.9.1 emitting NaN for `gpu_utilization` under certain probe timing -> scaler interpreted as zero -> desired replicas 0 -> router fallback loop.

eng-manager-liz: Thanks team. Postmortem requested, target: 48h draft. Also schedule a 1hr async review to decide mitigation (circuit breaker + validation in scaler + stricter router fallback heuristics).

cs-eli: I'll send customer notes once the postmortem draft is ready.

ops-runbook-bot: FOLLOW-UP TASK CREATED • Ticket ENG-1209 assigned to eng-runtime: "exporter emits NaN -> autoscaler misread".

alejandra: Closing thread for now. If anything regresses re-open incident. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
